the exact fixed-cache component arithmetic for weight, one pattern table and selective PWP vectors

verdict.recommended_label_for_current_cycles: pinned analytical output-tile recurrence estimates; strict is conservative in some modeled transfers but is not a hardware upper bound, and overlap is optimistic under two cache contexts
verdict.recommended_first_executable_target: q128/O1, SHARED96, SERIAL16, two explicit 32-KiB tile contexts plus two explicit 18-KiB descriptor banks

read_only_audit.method: Read-only source, contract and result review; independent integer capacity arithmetic; independent speedup redivision from pinned cycle totals; exact control-recurrence and causality audit.
read_only_audit.limitation: This hammer did not rebuild the 51.84-million-row M248/M338 phase population. The exact-work population was independently audited in M343/M340; M347 concentrates on the new M344 tiling, storage and schedule transformations.

capacity_recompute.formula_per_context_bytes: maximum_used_patterns * 144 * O PWP bytes + 16 * 96 * O weight bytes + q * 2 pattern bytes, with maximum_used_patterns=q for the frozen worst case.
capacity_recompute.finding: M344 correctly includes one output-tile weight set, one output-tile selective-PWP set and one q-entry pattern table in each worst-case cache context. All four pairs fit two equal 32-KiB cache contexts. The 64-KiB statement is therefore valid for the PWP/weight/pattern cache, not for total module SRAM; the separately declared descriptor SRAM raises fixed physical allocation to 101,536 bytes.

descriptor_audit.logical_sufficiency: The fields are sufficient to identify a raw row, selected center and exact Hamming distance under a per-context phase tag. original16 plus a resident center is sufficient to reconstruct the signed correction; distance is checking metadata rather than the correction itself.
unpriced_or_undefined: whether all 3000 rows or only assignment_rows are actually materialized
writes for fallback and zero rows even though packer cycles charge only assignment_rows
descriptor read bandwidth while eight output tiles replay the same rows
bank conflicts, context tag/phase metadata, ECC and address generation
the exact relationship between flags7 and correction sign/mask generation
descriptor_audit.finding: Descriptor bit capacity is adequate, but it is not yet an executable descriptor memory microarchitecture.

pattern_load_audit.finding: Pattern code is loaded once in matcher_packer before the first match, then q*2 pattern bytes are included again in candidate_tile_bytes for every output tile. The latter charges are duplicates because the pattern table is output-block independent and the capacity model stores only one copy per context.
pattern_load_audit.effect: The defect is conservative for candidate cycles: removing duplicate pattern transfers can only leave cycles unchanged or reduce them. It does not invalidate the capacity fit. It does invalidate the published cycle totals as an exact implementation of the stated one-pattern-table residency policy.

q128_pattern_decharge_interval.strict_explanation: One q128 pattern-table duplicate in the first tile is serialized for every phase, removing at least 138,240 cycles. At most all eight duplicate tile loads bind, removing 1,105,920 cycles.
q128_pattern_decharge_interval.overlap_explanation: Only the ten initial first-tile loads are unconditionally exposed in the ten per-sample replays; other duplicate load cycles may be hidden by max terms. The interval is arithmetic sensitivity, not a corrected executable-cycle claim.

two_context_schedule_audit.cache_ownership_conflict: For O1, current-partition compute and next-current-tile prefetch can occupy both cache contexts. Overlapping the next partition first-tile load with the whole current body requires either a third tile context, an explicit release point during the final tile, or a more detailed banked allocation. None is modeled.
two_context_schedule_audit.pattern_ownership_conflict: Even the strict recurrence overlaps next matcher_packer, including its pattern DMA, with current body. If pattern storage belongs to the declared two cache contexts, no free context is guaranteed while current tiling alternates both slots. A separate pattern SRAM or delayed matcher start must be explicit.
two_context_schedule_audit.finding: Strict is conservatively serialized for next first-tile load but omits resource conflicts and descriptor service, so it is not a rigorous hardware cycle upper bound. Overlap additionally assumes storage concurrency that two contexts do not generally provide and is an optimistic recurrence estimate.

resource_fairness_audit.what_is_fixed: worst-case PWP bytes per output tile, q*144*O = 18,432 bytes
what_is_not_fixed: matcher PE count: SYSTOLIC_Q grows from 16 to 128 distance PEs
candidate-only WIDE144 PWP path versus SHARED96
descriptor SRAM ports and replay bandwidth
resource_fairness_audit.finding: q*O=128 is a useful memory-tiling invariant, not an area or throughput normalization. The q128 wide+systolic point hides both a 128-PE matcher and a 144-byte candidate PWP path. The q128 SHARED96+SERIAL16 strict value, 1.396406x, is the more credible implementation seed, but remains non-executable until the serial matcher and finite SRAM schedule are realized.

p1.title: Pattern data is charged once before matching and again in every tile load
p1.impact: The M344 cycle totals do not exactly implement the stated one-pattern-table residency policy. q128 adds up to 1,105,920 raw duplicate DRAM service cycles.

p1.title: The overlap recurrence is not legal under the declared two tile contexts
p1.impact: Current-tile compute plus next-current-tile prefetch may consume both contexts; next-partition first-tile prefetch needs a third slot or an exact release point. The 2.038802x point is not an executable bound.

p1.title: Descriptor memory is capacity-priced but not service-priced
p1.impact: The model reserves one 48-bit entry per raw row but packer cycles cover only PWP assignment rows; fallback writes, eight-tile reads, banks and ports are undefined.

p1.title: Fixed q times O does not area-match matcher and port resources
p1.impact: q128 systolic has 8x the distance PEs of SERIAL16 and WIDE144 has 1.5x the PWP payload width of SHARED96. Peak speedup rows are not area normalized.

p1.title: Cycle-bound terminology exceeds the proof
p1.impact: The strict recurrence contains conservative serialization but omits conflicts and finite queues; overlap contains optimistic concurrency. Neither is a rigorous hardware upper/lower bound.

p2.title: Fixed-64-KiB naming excludes the separate descriptor SRAM
p2.impact: M344 does disclose 36,000 descriptor bytes, but paper-facing text must call 64 KiB the tile cache and state 101,536 bytes of fixed cache-plus-descriptor allocation.

p2.title: Per-phase binding and component sums are not retained
p2.impact: Exact correction of duplicate loads and diagnosis of which transfer is exposed require rerunning the full producer instead of inspecting the result.

p2.title: Phase tags and pattern/descriptor ownership are implicit
p2.impact: The 48-bit row descriptor is sufficient only with separately defined context tags, center-table validity, lowest-index tie policy and correction-generation semantics.

required_cycle_state: per tile-cache slot: EMPTY, PATTERN_LOADING, TILE_LOADING, READY, COMPUTING and RELEASED
per descriptor bank: EMPTY, MATCHING, PACKING, READY, REPLAYING and RELEASED
explicit context, phase, output-tile and generation tags
one 32-byte-per-cycle DMA request/response service with PATTERN, WEIGHT and PWP kinds
pattern table loaded exactly once per phase and an explicit physical residence location
finite matcher-to-descriptor, DMA-to-cache and compute-to-commit queues
one shared 96-byte compute port with weight latency one and PWP service two cycles
bank/port arbitration and backpressure on every interface
minimum_events: accept and match all 3000 raw16 rows
commit exactly one 48-bit descriptor for every row
load one output tile's weight and only its used PWP vectors
replay all descriptors for output block 0 through 7
release cache slots only after last consumer
commit all 3000x8 outputs and retire the phase
mandatory_assertions: pattern DMA occurs exactly once per phase
PWP DMA cannot accept before match_done and used-pattern bitmap commit
a tile cannot compute before weight and all selected PWP payloads are resident
a cache or descriptor context cannot be overwritten before release
every accepted raw row produces exactly one descriptor
descriptor center_id is below q and ties select the lowest center_id
PWP plus correction work exactly conserves candidate vector work
all eight output blocks consume the same immutable descriptor generation
queue or capacity pressure stalls; it never silently overlaps or drops work
required_comparisons: M344 SHARED96+SERIAL16 strict recurrence at 389416990 cycles
pattern-in-tile-cache versus explicit small pattern-SRAM sensitivity
minimum_next_finite_context_module_simul.promotion_gate: Only zero-mismatch cycles from this finite-state simulator, with explicit cache ownership and common baseline resources, may replace the 1.396406x analytical seed.

dc_dse.technology_and_constraint: same TSMC28 3.0-ns logic-only, ideal-clock and zero-wire-load pre-macro convention as the current Synopsys receipts

dc_dse.selection_rule: Choose the smallest PE point that sustains the finite-context simulator's required matcher rate at the same clock. Recompute candidate and bit-sparse throughput after giving both designs the same area and memory-port budget.
